title: Portal, command line and declared infrastructure: three doors, one API

videos.script: There are three ways to make something in Azure. Click it in the portal, type it on a command line, or describe it in a file. {{doors}} They feel like three products. They are three clients of one API, and each one ends in the same request. {{put}} You will build the shop's network three ways. First as a command, which runs once, now. {{cli}} Then as a Bicep file and a Terraform file. Each says what should exist, not what to do. {{files}} Run them twice, and the second time there is nothing to do. {{twice}} You will compile the Bicep, turn the template back into Bicep, and watch what gets lost on the way. {{decompile}} Then both tools reach the step they cannot take here: comparing the file with what really exists. {{whatif}} That comparison is where drift shows up: a change somebody made by hand, which the next deployment undoes. {{drift}} By the end, you can say which door fits which job, and why the file is the one that lasts. {{end}}
